text: Imagine the Moon moved toward Earth.
You are on the beach on a calm afternoon. The Moon is a pale disc above the sea.
Its pull lifts the oceans twice a day. Here, the tide rises about one metre.
But that pull grows fast. Halve the distance, and it becomes eight times stronger.
Half the distance. One hundred and ninety-two thousand kilometres.
The Moon looks twice as wide. And the sea comes in, fast.
High tide climbs the whole beach, all the way to the sea wall.
One third of the distance. Twenty-seven times the pull.
Now the sea pulls back. Hundreds of metres. The sea floor lies bare.
And then the water comes back…
…over the beach, over the boulevard, up to the doors of the hotels.
Above it all, the Moon is now four times as wide as today.
And it is still getting closer.
